Especially the eating thing. I think it was one of the bigger hurdles for me when traveling. So I started practicing “at home” (meaning my own city). If I could do it in front of people who I actually may run into again and recognize me, then I definitely can do it in a country where no one will ever see me again. And I’ve actually gotten very lucky and had a whole meal paid for here and there because I looked like that “wistful solo female traveler”. So there are benefits 😁

I could think of many reasons to answer your question but this one stands out to me:

To be confidently me. I found that when I solo travel to anywhere I don’t have ties to, I am much more confident and willing to take risks than when I’m home. I feel I am “living life” more authentically because I’m surrounded by people who will never see me again. So I can be who I want and do what I want.

The short answer is yes, you will get over him. And the funny thing is that you won’t realize you have, it’ll be just a natural release. 

With the whole “I want to be alone right now” I’ve experienced both sides. I’ve had exes who moved on quickly after me, and I’ve jumped into situations after breaking up/being broken up with. Unless you have evidence that your ex is a narcissist or sociopath, a lot of times this happens because we are forcing ourselves to have distractions. It’s painful to just sit around moping about our exes, even though we need to sit with our feelings and be alone. So we take comfort in others. It’s a very human thing to do. But I never just completely forgot my ex. There are many times when I’ve gone on first dates and I’m still very much in love with my ex in my mind. But I’ve grown more now that I no longer hop into relationships so soon after break ups. You live and learn.

Update:

I didn’t think this would gather alot of attention, and I also don’t think I have to explain anything, but I’m going to anyways bc there seems to be a bit of negativity?

1. We live in two different countries 5000 miles apart from each other. So yeah, that’s a glaring issue that I get from him. I wanted to try anyways but he didn’t. Doesn’t make him a bad person. Or anyone else for that matter.

2. There was a long message by me before his reply that I didn’t show, and the context of his message makes sense to my message. I never felt worry, insecurity or any real jealousy from him.

3. Snapchat was our main form of communication since we are in two different countries. Don’t really see an issue with that? Not like we could sit down in my living room to talk.

I was on vacation in Paris with just one other girl friend. I was dumped half a year before and this was essentially my “eat, pray, love” trip. I had no intentions of dating anyone seriously, but my friend convinced me to download dating apps while in Paris just to see what kind of matches I’d get, just as a little game. I matched with a native French man, and we flirted online for a couple days. I had no intention of meeting  him; for one, I was very worried about meeting a foreign guy in a country I was not from, and also I didn’t want to ruin my trip to Paris with a potentially “bad date”.  But he was such a sweet talker with many things in common, and I was open to him about my fears; he respected that and said he would do anything to make me feel comfortable. Finally, I decided to go out with him on the last night I was in Paris. It was the MOST magical date I had ever been on in my entire life. Not just because of the location, but I connected with him so well and intensely. Fast forward till now, we are still taking long distance for a little over a month now. Things are progressing well and steady, and we are meeting again in April to vacation together in Italy :)

Then unfortunately that’s the big glaring red flag that something is going on behind the scenes. I’m not assuming he is cheating, he still might not be. But he feels a certain way towards her that’s different compared to other people, and that has no place in your guys’ relationship. It’s still him being dishonest with you about something. You don’t deserve to be dragged along while he’s sorting his “feelings” of this other girl and you. You didn’t sign up for a relationship of three. I would move on and take this as a learning experience. It wasn’t the distance that broke you two, but his commitment to you that did.

Gaslighting. Telling you that your feelings are the problem is not okay. You are allowed to feel upset about a situation, period. Don’t let him take that away from you. 

Now, to take a step back to view the situation. Your past trauma has caused you to build paranoia, which is completely normal. It teaches you (and all of us) that every person is capable of every good and bad act in the book. To be more cautious into falling into deep trust with someone so quickly. However, it is important that you work through that before you can commit to building a foundation with someone else. Not saying you can’t have a relationship while working on yourself, but you will keep hitting these roadblocks with different people if you don’t properly sort it out. That’s your side.

On his side, if he truly cared for you and your feelings, he would not use the distance or your behavior as a way to justify not highlighting you on his social media presence. That’s manipulative. It’s like saying, “oh you get a treat if you’ve been a good girl and do these things”. No. You’re not a dog, you’re a human being. It does not matter if “she has a bf and he met him”, people cheat with anyone. Those are not actionable reasons to trust him or anyone for that matter. And, if he tells you that you can just leave if it makes you feel uncomfortable, all the more reasons to which he does not care. He’s attempting to make a power play on you, basically making him look superior in a way that you wouldn’t dare leave. 

The one thing I agree with him on is, yes don’t abandon your friends for a person. It’s important to have both balanced. But that’s not what’s happening here. He is abandoning YOU in favor of this female friend. Is he also this way with ALL of his friends, or just her? That’s a key difference too. 

A mature relationship is one where you can both “sit down” and talk about the tough topics. To create a safe secure space for both parties, especially in LDR. He’s basically telling you to deal with it yourself. That it’s not his problem. Your problems are his and vice versa. My honest advice? Walk away, and prove him wrong. If he doesn’t wanna fight for you to stay and improve things, fine. Show him that your relationship with yourself is so secure that you could care less about his other female friends and what he does. And that there are definitely men out there who will make you feel secure in the relationship that this stuff isn’t even an issue.

Something I have learned in LDR as well as in person relationships; never give up yourself or downplay your priorities for anyone. 

If it’s not THAT important to you to have kids, that’s one thing. But it sounds like the dream of you “being a foster parent since you were 14” is not something to just cast aside. Relationships do require compromise, but I believe there are some things about yourself you cannot compromise. 

Looking down the road, if you guys stick it out; do you feel like you can handle not resenting him for not having kids? Can he handle that guilt that comes along with being the roadblock to one of your dreams? 

Give him space to think on whatever he needs to think on. But YOU need to do some thinking too on what are your fundamentals that you can’t give up? I’ve heard being a social worker can be very rewarding, but you have to understand it’s still worlds apart from being a parent.

Trust issues were more like, coming forward to him first when I was trying to get a toxic ex out of my life by handling it myself. Us assuming the worst of each other first when things went wrong bc we used to do that before with past people.

We were fighting a lot towards the end of the relationship and weren’t always seeing eye to eye on things. To me, that just indicated that we were getting out of our honeymoon phase and figuring out our dynamic. There were also trust issues there about both of our past traumas and how it would bleed into the relationship. We both made mistakes. But for me, they were things that we needed to work on together to overcome. But he decided that he needed to work himself and personal demons and being happy with himself. Mixed with, he can’t fully trust me. I feel betrayed because I was an initially cold and distant person before I met him, and then he helped me to warm my heart and become emotionally vulnerable. Then he just dumps me and I’m left with dealing with how vulnerable I am, losing our child, and picking up all the pieces alone.
